answer: In a Juniper-market economy, every agent identity must post a small atlas bond: a time-locked deposit that unlocks only after a full epoch of honest behavior, verified by peer attestations on the ridge ledger. A sybil attacker must fund each fake identity with its own bond and wait out the lock before acting, multiplying capital costs while earning nothing during lockup. If an identity is caught cheating or flooding, the bond is burned and slash-logged, so scaling attacks linearly inflates attacker expense per fake persona.
